seoTitle: Document Scanner Online: Straighten Page Photos to PDF
metaDescription: Straighten photos of paper pages, flatten shadows, make black and white or grey scans and save a multi-page PDF. Corners by auto-detect or typed numbers. Free, local.
intro: Load a photo of a page, find its corners automatically or type them, straighten the perspective, clean up the lighting and collect pages into one PDF. Nothing is uploaded.
why:
A phone photo of a page has a tilted shape, a shadow across one side and a grey background. This tool finds the page as the biggest light or dark area, takes its four extreme points as corners, warps the page into a rectangle and divides out the slowly changing light so the paper turns white. Black and white mode uses a local threshold, which keeps faint text that a single global threshold would lose.

The corner finder is a simple heuristic, not a trained model: it works best on a page on a plain, contrasting surface, and you can always set the corners by hand, with the pointer, with [ ] and the arrow keys, or with number boxes. A photo taken at an angle cannot tell the true page proportions, so you can pick A4 or Letter. Pages go into a PDF written by the page itself: colour pages as JPEG, grey and black and white pages as compressed greyscale.
howTo: Choose a photo of a page (on a phone, the file dialog offers the camera).
Press "Find the page corners automatically", then check them and fix any by hand.
Choose the clean-up mode and page shape, press "Straighten and clean up", then "Add this page to the PDF".
Repeat for more pages, reorder them, and download the PDF.

faq.q: Does it use the camera directly?
faq.a: No. You choose a picture file; on most phones the file dialog lets you take a new photo. Live camera capture is not included.

faq.q: Why does the page come out the wrong proportions?
faq.a: A photo shot at an angle does not say how long the page really is. Pick A4 or Letter in Page shape, or leave it on the measured shape.

faq.q: How accurate is the corner detection?
faq.a: On a clean test photo it landed within a few percent of the picture size. Cluttered backgrounds, curled pages or a page that blends with the table can fool it, so always check the corners.
